Cache

Edge cache — 5 minutes

This path is configured to be cached at the Cloudflare edge for 300 seconds (5 minutes). Within that window every visitor is served the cached copy without hitting the origin.

Reload a few times: the first request is MISS, then HIT with age climbing toward 300. After ~5 min the edge revalidates and age resets.

How the 5-minute TTL is set

The origin (Apache) sends a Cloudflare-specific edge-TTL header on this path, and a Cache Rule makes the HTML eligible for caching:

# Apache (apache/pimenta-cache-headers.conf)
<Location "/cache/edge-5min/">
    Header set Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control "max-age=300"   # edge TTL = 5 min
    Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate"  # browser always revalidates
</Location>
# Cloudflare dashboard: Caching -> Cache Rules
When incoming requests match:  URI Path starts with  /cache/edge-5min/
Then:  Eligible for cache = Cache eligible (Cache everything)
       Edge TTL = Use cache-control header if present
  • Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control sets the edge TTL only — the browser TTL comes from Cache-Control.
  • HTML is not cached by default; the Cache Rule ("Cache everything") makes this page cacheable.
